About

Forecasts that survive contact with reality.

Prince George is a Workforce Management professional with over nine years of experience optimizing contact-center operations — specializing in forecasting, scheduling, capacity planning, and workforce analytics across global operations.

Most recently, as Senior Analyst WFM at American Express Global Business Travel, he administered NICE IEX workforce management activities end to end, improved forecast accuracy, reduced SLA risk, and established scalable scheduling strategies across internal, shared-services, and outsourced teams. He now works as a Workforce Management Specialist at ARRISE, based in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE.

With a focus on data-driven workforce strategy, he has collaborated with global stakeholders to align workforce planning with business objectives — enhancing efficiency through KPI improvement initiatives, scenario planning, and structured mentoring programs that grow the next generation of analysts.

Why Workforce Management?

The pull toward planning, not just reporting.

Workforce Management sits at an unusual intersection — half business strategy, half applied statistics, and entirely dependent on getting the human side right. That combination is what has kept nine-plus years interesting rather than repetitive.

Forecasting appeals because it rewards rigor: volume, shrinkage, and seasonality either add up to a believable number or they don't, and the difference shows up fast in service levels. Planning is the natural next step — translating that number into a roster that real people can actually work.

Analytics matters because a forecast or a schedule is only as good as the data behind it — which is why reporting, MIS, and dashboards have been a constant thread across every role since 2016, not an afterthought.

The handbook grew out of the same instinct: nine years of lessons that would have been useful to have on day one, written down for the next analyst starting theirs.

Career Story

Six roles, one thread: getting the right people on the floor at the right time.

My Journey

Started in 2016 running day-to-day workforce reporting for an ~800-person operation at Karvy.

How My Thinking Evolved

Moved from reactive reporting toward proactive forecasting and scenario planning as roles progressed.

Business Challenges

Scaling scheduling consistently across internal, shared-services, and outsourced teams at once.

Solutions

Rolling capacity strategies, standardised scheduling processes, and NICE IEX administration end to end.

Professional Growth

From WFM Executive to Senior Analyst to an international Workforce Management Specialist role.

Current Focus

Applying that experience at ARRISE, UAE — and sharing it through a published WFM handbook.
